To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new adaptive discrete-time inverse model controller that uses Generalized Sampling and Holding Functions and that overcomes the problems of the classical ZOH-based adaptive inverse model control.

the use of Generalized Sampling and Holds in an adaptive inverse model control scheme allows obtaining a discrete plant model with all its zeros in the stability region and allows performing an exact inversion of the plant, in comparison to the usual ZOH that only allows an approximate inversion of unstable systems.

the adaptive inverse model control scheme using generalized sampling and hold functions allows overcoming the difficulties that appear in the classical adaptive inverse model control schemes when a ZOH (zero-order hold) is used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new adaptive discrete-time inverse control scheme for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems using Generalized Sampling Hold Functions.
the development of an adaptive inverse model based control law for a system with uncertain parameters using a discrete implementation of the controller.
the development of an adaptive discrete-time inverse model based control strategy for systems with parametric uncertainty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed adaptive control scheme is a very promising and useful tool for controlling uncertain systems with unstable zeros.

the proposed method is able to overcome the difficulties associated with the presence of unstable zero dynamics in both the continuous time and the discrete-time models, and also the appearance of unstable discretized zeros.

the use of generalized sampling and hold functions in the implementation of the inverse model control scheme allows to overcome the difficulties associated to the presence of parametric uncertainties and unstable zeros in the system model and to obtain a discrete-time inverse model of the system which is more accurate than the usual one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a digital implementation of the inverse model scheme for a class of plants with unstable zeros.
we have developed an adaptive inverse model controller for a system with unknown parameters and with unstable zeros.

, in the presence of parametric uncertainty and unstable zeros, the use of Generalized Sampling and hold functions in the adaptive inverse model control scheme allows obtaining a better performance in comparison to the classical use of ZOH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed control scheme can be used in a wide variety of applications in the presence of parametric uncertainties.

the use of Generalized Sampling and hold functions in the implementation of inverse model based controllers is a promising approach to overcome the difficulties related to parametric uncertainty, and the appearance of unstable zeros in both the continuous-time plant and the discrete-time model.
the proposed adaptive control scheme can be applied to a wider range of systems than the classical inverse model control schemes.
